---
title: "{{< fa list-check >}} Before the workshop"
---

Six steps. Steps 1 to 3 are about your own work and your own thinking, and they are the ones the day depends on. Steps 4 to 6 are setup and admin.

Work through them in order. Steps 1 and 2 have no due date because you bring the result with you; the other four have due dates so that problems surface while there is still time to fix them.

| Step | What | Due |
|------|------|-----|
| [1](01-bring-your-data.qmd) | Bring a piece of your own data | bring it with you |
| [2](02-publishing-steps.qmd) | Write down how you publish a paper | bring it with you |
| [3](03-declaration-reading.qmd) | Read the AI declaration questionnaires | {{< var due.reading >}} |
| [4](04-install-claude-code.qmd) | Install Claude Code | before Step 5 |
| [5](05-verify-setup.qmd) | Test your setup | {{< var due.setup >}} |
| [6](06-survey.qmd) | Complete the pre-course survey | {{< var due.survey >}} |

: {tbl-colwidths="[10,55,35]"}

::: {.callout-tip}
## How long will this take?

Steps 1 and 2 are thinking, not typing: half an hour each if you already know which dataset you want to use. Step 3 is about an hour of reading. Steps 4 to 6 are around half an hour together, unless something goes wrong with the install, which is exactly why Step 5 has a due date a week before the workshop.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## If you get stuck

Do not spend an evening fighting an install. Open an issue on your setup repository (Step 5 explains how) or email [{{< var email >}}](mailto:{{< var email >}}?subject=agentsforsci setup). Getting you unstuck before the day is the whole point of having pre-work.
:::
